framework.name: National Standards for Personal Financial Education

objectives.description: Explain how education and skills affect earning potential, using data on careers.
Read a pay stub and explain gross pay, net pay and each deduction.
Calculate take-home pay from an hourly wage and a salary.
Describe how federal and state income tax works and complete a simple tax form.
Create a monthly budget that separates needs from wants.
Compare prices and unit costs to make a purchasing decision.
Explain how advertising and peers influence spending.
Explain why an emergency fund matters and set a savings goal.
Compare savings accounts, checking accounts and certificates of deposit.
Calculate simple and compound interest and compare the results.
Describe stocks, bonds and mutual funds and the relationship of risk and return.
Explain the benefit of investing early using compound growth.
Describe how credit cards and loans work and calculate the cost of borrowing.
Explain a credit score and what raises or lowers it.
Describe types of insurance and explain what each protects against.
Recognize scams and identity theft and describe how to protect yourself.
Compare the costs and benefits of college, trade school and work after graduation.
Create a personal financial plan for the first year after high school.
